correctnessFindings.assessment: Backpressure accounts for retained UTF-16 text, entry overhead, and outstanding socket write bytes. It applies 4 MiB/1 MiB global high/low watermarks and 64 KiB/32 KiB per-session watermarks, with owner checks protecting replacement clients.

The stream pause owner is independent of the prior client pause timeout. The existing five-second client failsafe cannot resume a producer while stream backpressure remains asserted. Detach, disconnect, and control replacement retire their pressure ownership and permit resumption.

Native PTY pause/resume controls reading from the PTY endpoint. When a viewer stays connected but never drains, the producer can remain paused indefinitely, and the child can block after native output buffers fill. This is a progress and latency tradeoff, not evidence that the process exited.

Existing background keep-tail dropping remains the data-loss policy for droppable traffic. Unsupported pause handles retain the existing 32 MiB write-through safety valve; the new user-space target is not a universal native-memory bound.

originalReview.userVisibleBeforeAfter: A terminal with a stalled stream previously allowed retained output to grow. It now slows or stops the terminal producer until the stream drains or its owner detaches. A permanently stalled viewer can therefore stop command progress indefinitely.
originalReview.capacityAndDataLoss: No new terminal scrollback capacity or output-drop threshold is introduced here. Applying persistent backpressure trades producer progress for retained output memory. Native buffers and unsupported-pause fallback behavior remain outside a strict global bound.

platformEvidence.assessment: The reviewed host/session wrappers use PTY pause/resume rather than POSIX signals. POSIX PTY and Windows ConPTY both expose endpoint reads, but their native buffering and producer-blocking behavior need target-platform validation. Existing real TCP reproduction uses a callback producer honoring pause; it does not execute a native Windows, Linux, or macOS PTY.
platformEvidence.executedHost: Fresh shared batch: macOS darwin arm64; Node 26.6.0. PRs outside that batch have no new execution in this follow-up.

originalReview.sshAndFolderCases: Pressure belongs to the daemon/session on the execution host and the current client owner. A disconnected or stalled SSH path does not establish process death. Folder workspaces use the same terminal ownership and require no Git metadata.

regressionCoverage.description: Published tests cover accounting, small writes, owner replacement, socket drain, stale refill callbacks, and session pause controls. The historical real TCP artifact demonstrates bounded 8 MiB producers that resume after drain; visible 64 KiB/1 KiB and hidden cases are documented.

regressionCoverage.limitations: No new native PTY execution was performed in this review. A finite drain test cannot establish eventual progress for a client that never drains. Watermarks bound selected user-space ownership, not all kernel, PTY, or renderer memory.
